requirements.heading: Conformance requirement terminology
requirements.text: An implementation is not compliant if it fails to satisfy one or more of the MUST requirements for the protocols it implements.

requirements.heading: Conformance requirement terminology
requirements.text: An implementation that satisfies all the MUST and all the SHOULD requirements for its protocols is said to be "unconditionally compliant"; one that satisfies all the MUST requirements but not all the SHOULD requirements for its protocols is said to be "conditionally compliant."

requirements.heading: The Content-Location Header
requirements.text: However, URI-s in Content-Location headers (if absolute, or resolvable to absolute URIs) SHOULD still be globally unique.

requirements.heading: URIs of MHTML aggregates
requirements.text: If a Content-Location header field is used in the heading of a multipart/related, this Content-Location SHOULD apply to the whole aggregate, not to its root part.

requirements.heading: Encoding of URIs containing inappropriate characters
requirements.text: This encoding MUST only be done in the header, not in the HTML text.

requirements.heading: Encoding of URIs containing inappropriate characters
requirements.text: Receiving clients MUST decode the [MIME3] encoding in the heading before comparing URIs in body text to URIs in Content-Location headers.

requirements.heading: Encoding of URIs containing inappropriate characters
requirements.text: The charset parameter value "US-ASCII" SHOULD be used if the URI contains no octets outside of the 7-bit range.

requirements.heading: Encoding of URIs containing inappropriate characters
requirements.text: If such octets are present, the correct charset parameter value (derived e.g. from information about the HTML document the URI was found in) SHOULD be used.

requirements.heading: Encoding of URIs containing inappropriate characters
requirements.text: If this cannot be safely established, the value "UNKNOWN-8BIT" [RFC 1428] MUST be used.

requirements.heading: Encoding of URIs containing inappropriate characters
requirements.text: Note, that for the matching of URIs in text/html body parts to URIs in Content-Location headers, the value of the charset parameter is irrelevant, but that it may be relevant for other purposes, and that incorrect labeling MUST, therefore, be avoided.

requirements.heading: Folding of long URIs
requirements.text: Encoding as discussed in clause 4.4.1 MUST be done before such folding.

requirements.heading: Base URIs for resolution of relative URIs
requirements.text: (e) When the methods above do not yield an absolute URI, a base URL of "thismessage:/" MUST be employed.

requirements.heading: Sending documents without linked objects
requirements.text: If a text/html resource (object) is sent without subsidiary resources, to which it refers, it MAY be sent by itself.

requirements.heading: Use of the Content-Type "multipart/related"
requirements.text: If a message contains one or more MIME body parts containing URIs and also contains as separate body parts, resources, to which these URIs (as defined, for example, in HTML 2.0 [HTML2]) refer, then this whole set of body parts (referring body parts and referred-to body parts) SHOULD be sent within a multipart/related structure as defined in [REL].

requirements.heading: Use of the Content-Type "multipart/related"
requirements.text: When the start body part of a multipart/related structure is an atomic object, such as a text/html resource, it SHOULD be employed as the root resource of that multipart/related structure.

requirements.heading: Use of the Content-Type "multipart/related"
requirements.text: When the start body part of a multipart/related structure is a multipart/alternative structure, and that structure contains at least one alternative body part which is a suitable atomic object, such as a text/html resource, then that body part SHOULD be employed as the root resource of the aggregate document.

requirements.heading: Use of the Content-Type "multipart/related"
requirements.text: In addition, if the multipart/related start object is not the first body part in a multipart/related structure, [REL] further requires that its Content-ID MUST be specified as the value of a start parameter in the "Content-Type: multipart/related" header.

requirements.heading: Use of the Content-Type "multipart/related"
requirements.text: When a sending MUA sends objects which were retrieved from the WWW, it SHOULD maintain their WWW URIs.

requirements.heading: Use of the Content-Type "multipart/related"
requirements.text: It SHOULD not transform these URIs into some other URI form prior to transmitting them.

requirements.heading: Use of the Content-Type "multipart/related"
requirements.text: Within a multipart/related structure, each body part MUST have, if assigned, a different Content-ID header value and a Content-Location header field values which resolve to a different URI.

requirements.heading: Use of the Content-ID header and CID URLs
requirements.text: When URIs employing a CID (Content-ID) scheme as defined in [URL] and [MIDCID] are used to reference other body parts in an MHTML multipart/related structure, they MUST only be matched against Content-ID header values, and not against Content-Location header with CID: values.

requirements.heading: Use of the Content-ID header and CID URLs
requirements.text: Note: Content-IDs MUST be globally unique [MIME1].

requirements.heading: Character encoding issues and end-of-line issues
requirements.text: In sending a message, all the above mentioned mechanisms MAY be used, and any mixture of them MAY occur when sending the document in MIME format.

requirements.heading: Character encoding issues and end-of-line issues
requirements.text: Receiving user agents (together with any Web browser they may use to display the document) MUST be capable of handling any combinations of these mechanisms.

requirements.heading: Character encoding issues and end-of-line issues
requirements.text: - The MIME standard [MIME2] requires that e-mailed documents of "Content-Type: Text/ MUST be in canonical form before a Content- Transfer-Encoding is applied, i.e. that line breaks are encoded as CRLFs, not as bare CRs or bare LFs or something else.

requirements.heading: Character encoding issues and end-of-line issues
requirements.text: If a document has to be converted in such a way that a checksum based message integrity check becomes invalid, then this integrity check header SHOULD be removed from the document.

requirements.heading: Character encoding issues and end-of-line issues
requirements.text: Because the default differs for different mechanisms, when HTML is transferred through e-mail, the charset parameter SHOULD be included, rather than relying on the default.

requirements.heading: Security considerations related to caching
requirements.text: When processing (rendering) a text/html body part in an MHTML multipart/related structure, all URIs in that text/html body part which reference subsidiary resources within the same multipart/related structure SHALL be satisfied by those resources and not by resources from any another local or remote source.

requirements.heading: Security considerations related to caching
requirements.text: Therefore, if a sender wishes a recipient to always retrieve an URI referenced resource from its source, an URI labeled copy of that resource MUST NOT be included in the same multipart/related structure.
